about: Concept engines: the kinds of idea a page can rest on, each with the corpus cards that run it. concept tags each of its seven worlds with one engine, the seven span at least four, and roll.mjs --engines deals three worlds from three different engines. An engine is a way an idea works, never a look; two worlds on one engine are one idea in two outfits. Engines named in references/patterns/house-tells.md are the plugin's own recent defaults and need a reason.

engines.name: The product performs
engines.gist: The page runs the thing it sells, so the visitor uses it instead of reading about it.
engines.trap: A demo pasted under a marketing hero; the performance has to be the argument, not an exhibit.

engines.name: The page is an artefact of the subject's world
engines.gist: The page takes the form of a printed or made thing the subject already produces or handles: a ticket, a deck, a catalogue, a shelf.
engines.trap: Any artefact of the category (a call sheet for any film studio, a proof for any design tool); the artefact must be this client's own.

engines.name: The name is the material
engines.gist: The client's name, read for what it means, supplies the behaviour or the system of the page.
engines.trap: The pun as a picture; the name has to make the visitor do something, not only see something.

engines.name: One motif drives everything
engines.gist: One shape, line or object from the subject becomes the button, the mask, the loader and the section edges.
engines.trap: A motif sprinkled as decoration; it must carry structure on every screen.

engines.name: Dressed as another category
engines.gist: The subject is sold in the clothes of an unrelated genre, played with total sincerity.
engines.trap: A costume chosen for novelty; the borrowed genre has to say something true about the subject.

engines.name: The place carries it
engines.gist: One real place, its light and its measurements, does the persuading; the page is a way of being there.
engines.trap: A full-bleed landscape with a serif headline, the luxury category's rut.

engines.name: One object on a held stage
engines.gist: A single object holds the screen while the content changes around it or on it.
engines.trap: A product turntable; the object has to change state as the argument advances.

engines.name: One section, one colour
engines.gist: Flat colour fields are the chapters, and the colour itself carries the subject's range or mood.
engines.trap: A rainbow of section backgrounds with nothing tying a colour to its content.

engines.name: The voice carries it
engines.gist: The copy is the design: a tone, a claim or a set of plain words held so consistently that the layout serves it.
engines.trap: Big type with nothing to say; the voice has to be this client's and no one else's.

engines.name: The visitor's act is the material
engines.gist: The visitor draws, switches, chooses or operates something, and the page answers with the subject's real content.
engines.trap: A playground of toys; one act, with the subject's real content behind it and a keyboard path.

engines.name: The collage that resolves into an index
engines.gist: The work or the people appear first as a gathering, and the gathering organises itself into something to browse.
engines.trap: A card grid with hover zoom; the arrangement has to mean something before it becomes a list.

engines.name: The process performed
engines.gist: The scroll performs the subject's real sequence, one step per chapter: a journey, a making, a growth.
engines.trap: Scroll as the engine of a physical process with a numeric readout beside it; see house-tells.md before choosing it.

engines.name: A world you enter
engines.gist: A rendered or painted world the visitor travels through, with the DOM as its mirror.
engines.trap: A 3D scene for its own sake; the world has to be the only place this subject could be met.

engines.name: The visitor is cast in a role
engines.gist: The page gives the visitor a part in the subject's world (operator, guest, member) and speaks to them in it.
engines.trap: A HUD costume on a page that is not technical; the role must come from who the audience really is.
